pack.title: Unsolicited life advice
pack.description: Love, expressed as instructions. Receive the love, decline the orders.

scenarios.setting: Phone call. Your parent, ten minutes into your career choices.
scenarios.jab: I'm just saying — at your age I already owned a house.

replies.line: Different market, same work ethic. I'm on my path.
replies.why: It names the real difference once, then closes with a fact that needs no defense.
replies.delivery: Pause, then say “Different market, same work ethic” at a steady, conversational volume. ” and avoid an economics debate unless you want one.

replies.why: It receives the message without receiving the assignment.
replies.delivery: Say “Noted” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. ” and avoid an economics debate unless you want one.

replies.line: I know — you set the bar high. I'm getting there my way.
replies.why: It recognizes your parent's experience while affirming that your own path can differ.
replies.delivery: Keep “I know” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. ” and avoid an economics debate unless you want one.

replies.line: My timeline has its own calendar.
replies.why: A light image distinguishes your path from someone else's schedule.
replies.delivery: Keep “My timeline has its own calendar” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. ” and avoid an economics debate unless you want one.

trap.line: Yeah well houses cost triple now, so thanks for nothing.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Discuss your plans without accepting an age comparison.

followUp.jab: You need to work harder if you want a house.
followUp.line: I'm working toward my own plan; advice is welcome when I ask for it.
followUp.why: It distinguishes your plan from unsolicited judgments about effort.
followUp.delivery: Keep your pace steady, emphasize “my own plan,” and avoid an economics debate unless you want one.

scenarios.setting: Family group chat. Your sibling, replying to your weekend plans.
scenarios.jab: Must be nice to have no responsibilities lol

replies.line: I'm enjoying my time off. I don't want to compare responsibilities.
replies.why: It affirms your plans while declining a competition over obligations.
replies.delivery: Keep the reply brief and warm; don't joke that you have no responsibilities.

replies.line: I know your week is full; I'd like to enjoy my weekend without the comparison.
replies.why: It recognizes their workload without accepting a dismissive judgment.
replies.delivery: Keep the reply brief and warm; don't joke that you have no responsibilities.

replies.line: My responsibilities approved this weekend's leave request.
replies.why: The joke claims a legitimate break rather than denying you have responsibilities.
replies.delivery: Keep the reply brief and warm; don't joke that you have no responsibilities.

replies.line: No comparisons about my time off, please.
replies.why: It states the immediate boundary without adding a personal judgment.
replies.delivery: Keep the reply brief and warm; don't joke that you have no responsibilities.

scenarios.goal: Respond to a dig about your free time.

followUp.jab: Some of us can't just take time off.
followUp.line: I understand; I don't want us comparing whose responsibilities count.
followUp.why: It acknowledges the difference without accepting a competition over obligations.
followUp.delivery: Keep the reply brief and warm; don't joke that you have no responsibilities.

scenarios.setting: A relative gives repeated advice about your relationship after you ask them to stop.
scenarios.jab: I'm just saying, you could do better.
scenarios.goal: Close an unwelcome discussion about your partner.

replies.line: I'm not asking for opinions about my relationship.
replies.why: It clarifies that the conversation is not an invitation for advice.
replies.delivery: Pause, then say “I'm not asking for opinions about my relationship” at a steady, conversational volume. ” and introduce another topic if useful.

replies.line: My relationship isn't up for review.
replies.why: It ends the evaluative discussion without attacking the relative.
replies.delivery: Say “My relationship isn't up for review” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. ” and introduce another topic if useful.

replies.line: I know you care; these comments aren't helpful, and I'd like us to change the subject.
replies.why: It acknowledges concern while asking for a concrete conversational change.
replies.delivery: Use a steady ending on “change the subject,” and introduce another topic if useful.

replies.line: The relationship review committee is on recess.
replies.why: A playful image closes the topic without inviting a vote.
replies.delivery: Keep “The relationship review committee is on recess” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. ” and introduce another topic if useful.

followUp.line: You can have your opinion; I don't want to discuss it.
followUp.why: It distinguishes their private opinion from your participation in the discussion.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “You can have your opinion,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.
